boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Pomona spaces for studying, making, gathering, art, and campus expression, with access cues grounded in College sources.

cards.title: Honnold-Mudd Library study rooms
cards.subtitle: Library study space
cards.notes: Use the study rooms for a focused work session, then keep conversation considerate of others sharing the library.
cards.short_summary: A documented study-room stop for solo work or meeting up with classmates.
cards.evidence_claim: A Pomona student tour guide says students study in Honnold-Mudd Library’s study rooms.
cards.source_title: Connect with a Tour Guide | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Library access and room-use rules may vary; check the library before planning a group session.

cards.title: Smith Campus Center Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Smith Campus Center outdoor gathering space
cards.notes: Meet at an umbrella table or use the courtyard as a waypoint between classes; it remains a public passage space.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor campus-center courtyard with seating and direct connections to student services.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes the courtyard as a public space with umbrella tables and chairs, with access to campus-center services.
cards.source_title: Smith Campus Center Spaces | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: The courtyard is public, but reserved events may be in progress; leave paths and service access open.

cards.title: Coop Fountain
cards.subtitle: Smith Campus Center food-service venue
cards.notes: Use the Fountain as a campus-center meetup point or food stop, and check current dining details before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A long-running food-service location inside the Smith Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona identifies the Coop Fountain as one of the food services on the Smith Campus Center’s main level.
cards.access_notes: Food and drink purchases are separate from simply passing through the Campus Center.

cards.entity_name: Rick and Susan Sontag Center for Collaborative Creativity (the Hive)
cards.title: The Hive
cards.subtitle: Maker and collaborative-creativity center
cards.notes: Drop in to explore a making activity or settle into a study session; ask staff about equipment and program access.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on creative space that also draws students looking for a welcoming place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says the Hive combines a hands-on maker space with design courses and that some students come there to study.
cards.source_title: An Update on the Hive and Its Next Chapter | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Confirm current workshop, equipment, and building-access arrangements with the Hive.

cards.title: Marston Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Central campus lawn
cards.notes: Bring a book or meet a friend on the lawn between classes, while yielding to any scheduled campus programming.
cards.short_summary: Pomona’s central quadrangle, used as both a green space and an event setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona identifies Marston Quadrangle as the center of campus, and its admissions materials place student activities there.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor common area; event setups may affect available lawn space.

cards.title: Walker Wall
cards.subtitle: Walker Beach free-speech wall
cards.notes: Read the current painted messages and, if you plan to contribute, follow the College’s wall guidance and community norms.
cards.short_summary: A campus forum where students use paint to share opinions and advertise events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says Walker Wall has served as a public forum for student expression and event advertising since the early 1970s.
cards.source_title: Traditions at Pomona College | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Painting is governed by College policies; review current guidance before adding anything.

cards.title: Victor Montgomery Music Library
cards.subtitle: Thatcher Music Building, Room 209
cards.notes: Use the study area, listening station, or seminar room for music-focused work, and check the posted library schedule first.
cards.short_summary: A music library with study seating, computers, listening resources, and space for small groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says the Montgomery Music Library has a study area, computer and listening stations, and a seminar room for study groups.
cards.source_title: Victor Montgomery Music Library | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: The College notes that hours are subject to change; verify access before heading over.

cards.title: Edmunds Ballroom
cards.subtitle: Smith Campus Center event space
cards.notes: Look for lectures, performances, or campus gatherings scheduled here, and use the room only when an event is open to you.
cards.short_summary: The Campus Center’s largest configurable venue for dining, audiences, and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona describes Edmunds Ballroom as the largest space in Smith Campus Center, with dining, audience, and performance setups.
cards.source_title: Smith Campus Center Spaces | Pomona College
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled events and reservations; do not enter during private programming.

cards.title: Mudd Lounge
cards.subtitle: Residential common-area lounge
cards.notes: Coordinate a recognized student gathering through the appropriate reservation process, and respect the residence-hall setting.
cards.short_summary: A residential common area available for organized academic, social, and co-curricular events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona’s housing policies list Mudd Lounge among residential spaces reservable for organized student events.
cards.source_title: HRL Policies and Procedures | Pomona College Catalog
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required for organized use; residential common-area events are substance-free.

cards.entity_name: James Turrell Skyspace, Dividing the Light
cards.title: James Turrell Skyspace
cards.subtitle: Draper Courtyard, Lincoln and Edmunds Buildings
cards.notes: Visit at a calm time to sit beneath the canopy and observe the sky; sunrise and sunset programs offer a longer experience.
cards.short_summary: A public art installation designed around changing light, sky, and quiet observation.
cards.evidence_claim: Pomona says the public may visit Dividing the Light anytime and describes daily sunrise and sunset lighting programs.
cards.access_notes: The Skyspace is public and not reservable; no food or drink is permitted, and visitors should respect quiet enjoyment.
